text: Responsibility for payment of wages: Every employer shall be responsible for the payment to persons employed by him of all wages required to be paid under this Act. In case of factories, industrial or other establishments, the person named as manager or person responsible to the employer for supervision and control shall be responsible for such payment.
Fixation of wage-periods: Every person responsible for the payment of wages under section 3 shall fix periods in respect of which such wages shall be payable. No wage-period shall exceed one month.

Time of payment of wages: The wages of every person employed upon or in any railway, factory or industrial or other establishment upon or in which less than one thousand persons are employed, shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day, and in any other establishment, shall be paid before the expiry of the tenth day, after the last day of the wage-period in respect of which the wages are payable. Where the employment of any person is terminated by or on behalf of the employer, the wages earned by him shall be paid before the expiry of the second working day from the day on which his employment is terminated.

Deductions which may be made from wages: The wages of an employed person shall be paid to him without deductions of any kind except those authorised by or under this Act. Deductions may be made only for fines, absence from duty, damage to or loss of goods expressly entrusted to the employed person, house-accommodation supplied by the employer, recovery of advances or loans, and income-tax or other statutory deductions.

Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages: The appropriate Government may appoint an authority to hear and decide all claims arising out of deductions from or delay in payment of the wages of persons employed. An application may be presented by the employed person himself, or any legal practitioner or authorized trade union official, or an Inspector. Every such application shall be presented within twelve months from the date on which the deduction from wages was made or from the date on which the payment of the wages was due to be made, provided that delay may be condoned on showing sufficient cause. The authority may direct refund of the deduction or payment of delayed wages, together with compensation.

Time limit for payment of wages: The employer shall pay or cause to be paid wages to the employees where employed on daily basis, at the end of the shift; on weekly basis, on the last working day of the week; on fortnightly basis, before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight; on monthly basis, before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month. Where an employee has been removed, dismissed, retrenched, resigned or became unemployed due to closure, wages shall be paid within two working days.

Claims under Code and procedure for determination thereof: The appropriate Government may appoint one or more authorities to hear and determine claims relating to minimum wages, payment of wages, and bonus. The employee concerned or any trade union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator may file an application before the Authority within a period of three years from the date on which the claim arose, provided delay may be condoned for sufficient cause.
